title: Tariffs Got Refunded. Why Didn't Prices Come Back Down?
summary: Explainer on why refunding the struck-down tariffs did not lower prices: refunds go to importers, the burden fell on Americans, and replacement tariffs keep restocking costs high.

assertions.quote: The New York Fed found nearly ninety percent of the burden of the twenty twenty-five tariffs fell on American firms and consumers.
If foreign sellers had carried the tax, they'd have cut their prices to make room for it. Mostly, they didn't.
Within seven months, shoppers were carrying about forty-five percent of the bill. The rest sat with American companies.
Dryers had no tariff on them. Their prices rose by about the same amount.
Each new factory job the tariff created cost shoppers over eight hundred thousand dollars a year.
Prices went up within days of a new tariff, before any tariffed stock had even arrived. Stores were pricing the next container.

verdicts.note: Daily price trackers saw some immediate increases on announcement, but most pass-through built gradually over months.

Retailers take a few months to pass on higher costs: only about half of the direct effect of a tariff is in consumer prices after three months and all of it by six, so retail prices do not jump at announcement.

Surveyed firms cited fixed-price contracts that prevent raising prices until expiry and a deliberate trickle-up strategy of gradual increases to avoid shocking customers, the opposite of pricing the next shipment at announcement.

assertions.quote: Their model has the tariffs still holding goods prices about two percent higher. That part doesn't fade.
But inflation is how fast prices rise, not where they are.
The refund paid back a cost importers had already carried. It didn't remove the cost of the next container.

verdicts.note: Prices track replacement cost; a refund of sunk duties is a windfall to the balance sheet while new tariffs keep the marginal import cost elevated.

assertions.quote: Customs is still collecting about twenty-three billion dollars a month. Before all this, in January twenty twenty-five, it was about eight.

verdicts.note: Monthly customs receipts after the ruling stayed several times their 2024 level as Section 122 and 232 tariffs replaced the emergency ones, though below the 2025 peak.
